To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best ordering strategy for the news genre combines chronological order of events with topical relatedness and that the ordering strategy has a significant impact on summary quality.

1) there is a significant amount of information in the news that can be ordered in multiple ways and 2) a simple strategy that combines chronological ordering and topical relatedness performs significantly better than two baseline ordering strategies.

(i) there is a high correlation between the order of events in a story and the order in which the events should appear in a summary, and (ii) there is a correlation between the topical relatedness of events and the order in a summary, but this correlation is not as strong as that of the chronological ordering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether there are general principles for ordering information in news articles and whether these principles can be used to improve the coherence of summaries.

the ordering of information is a very important factor in the generation of summaries, and that a strategy that combines constraints from both chronological order of events, and topical relatedness can improve the ordering of information for a multidocument summarization system.
the results of our experiments suggest that the ordering of sentences for the news genre can be inferred from the ordering of events and the topical similarity of sentences.
the ordering strategy proposed in this work is a significant improvement over baseline strategies and that it is a step in the right direction for the task of multidocument summarization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is feasible to use ordering constraints for the news genre, and that it is possible to develop a simple algorithm that can exploit such constraints.
the ordering of information in the news domain is a complex process and the use of a combination of constraints is required for effective summarization.
we have developed an algorithm that orders information in multidocument news summaries, and we have shown that the orderings generated are significantly better than two baseline algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of ordering information is a difficult problem that requires the use of multiple strategies.
the problem of ordering information is not trivial and that a combination of different constraints can improve the quality of the generated summaries.
